subject: AP Physics 1
stem: Cart X has mass 2 kg and moves at 6 m/s. Cart Y has mass 6 kg and moves at 2 m/s. Each cart is brought to rest by the same constant braking force. Which statement is correct?

choices.t: Both stop in the same time and travel the same distance, because their momenta are equal.
Y takes three times as long to stop and travels farther, because it has more mass.
X takes three times as long to stop and travels three times as far, because it moves three times as fast.
Both stop in the same time, but X travels three times as far.

subject: AP Physics 1
stem: Block P has mass 3 kg and moves at 8 m/s. Block Q has mass 12 kg and moves at 2 m/s. Each block is brought to rest by the same constant force. Which statement is correct?

choices.t: Both stop in the same time and travel the same distance, because their momenta are equal.
Q takes four times as long to stop and travels farther, because it has four times the mass.
P takes four times as long to stop and travels four times as far, because it moves four times as fast.
Both stop in the same time, but P travels four times as far.

subject: AP Physics 1
stem: A 500 kg car moves at 12 m/s and a 1500 kg truck moves at 4 m/s. Each is brought to rest over the same stopping distance by a constant braking force. How do the braking forces compare?

choices.t: The forces are equal, because the car and truck have the same momentum.
The force on the car is three times the force on the truck.
The force on the truck is three times the force on the car, because the truck has three times the mass.
The force on the car is nine times the force on the truck, because the car is three times as fast.

subject: AP Physics 1
stem: Block P has mass 1 kg and moves at 8 m/s. Block Q has mass 4 kg and moves at 4 m/s. The same constant force brings each block to rest. Which statement is correct?

choices.t: Q takes twice as long to stop, and both blocks travel the same distance.
Both blocks stop in the same time and travel the same distance, because their kinetic energies are equal.
P takes twice as long to stop, and both blocks travel the same distance.
Q takes twice as long to stop and travels twice as far, because it has twice the momentum.

subject: AP Physics 1
stem: A 0.50 kg clay ball and a 0.50 kg rubber ball each hit the same wall at 6.0 m/s, and each is in contact with the wall for the same time. The clay ball sticks to the wall. The rubber ball rebounds at 4.0 m/s. How do the average forces the wall exerts on the balls compare?

choices.t: The force on the rubber ball is about 1.7 times the force on the clay ball.
The forces are equal, because both balls arrive with the same momentum and the same contact time.
The force on the clay ball is about 3 times the force on the rubber ball, because the clay ball loses 6 m/s of speed and the rubber ball loses only 2 m/s.
The force on the clay ball is about 1.8 times the force on the rubber ball, because the clay ball loses 9 J of kinetic energy and the rubber ball loses 5 J.

subject: AP Physics 1
stem: A 0.20 kg clay ball and a 0.20 kg rubber ball each hit the same wall at 10 m/s, with equal contact times. The clay ball sticks. The rubber ball rebounds at 5 m/s. How do the average forces the wall exerts on the balls compare?

choices.t: The forces are equal, because both balls arrive with the same momentum and the same contact time.

The force on the clay ball is about 1.3 times the force on the rubber ball, because the clay ball loses 10 J of kinetic energy and the rubber ball loses 7.5 J.
The force on the rubber ball is 1.5 times the force on the clay ball.

subject: AP Physics 1
stem: A 1000 kg car hits a barrier at 6.0 m/s in two crash tests, each lasting the same time. In test 1 the car stops against the barrier. In test 2 the car rebounds at 2.0 m/s. How do the average forces on the car compare?

choices.t: The force in test 2 is about 1.3 times the force in test 1.
The forces are equal, because the car arrives at the same speed with the same contact time.
The force in test 1 is 1.5 times the force in test 2, because the car loses 6 m/s of speed in test 1 and only 4 m/s in test 2.

The force in trial 2 is 1.25 times the force in trial 1.

subject: AP Physics 1
stem: A 2 kg cart moving at +4 m/s collides with a 1 kg cart at rest on a frictionless track. Motion sensors show that afterward the 2 kg cart moves at +2 m/s and the 1 kg cart moves at +4 m/s. Which statement about this collision is correct?

choices.t: It is elastic, because the total momentum is the same before and after.
It is perfectly inelastic, because kinetic energy decreased.
It is inelastic but the carts do not stick: momentum is conserved while kinetic energy falls from 16 J to 12 J.
The data are impossible, because kinetic energy is not conserved.

subject: AP Physics 1
stem: A 3 kg cart moving at +5 m/s collides with a 2 kg cart at rest on a frictionless track. Afterward the 3 kg cart moves at +1 m/s and the 2 kg cart moves at +6 m/s. Which statement about this collision is correct?

choices.t: It is inelastic, because the 3 kg cart lost most of its speed.
It is elastic: momentum stays 15 kg·m/s and kinetic energy stays 37.5 J.
It is perfectly inelastic, because the 3 kg cart slows down a great deal.
The data are impossible, because the 2 kg cart ends up faster than the 3 kg cart started.

choices.t: It is elastic, because the total momentum is the same before and after.
It is inelastic but not perfectly inelastic, because the carts lose some kinetic energy.
It is perfectly inelastic: momentum is conserved while kinetic energy falls from 10 J to 2 J.
Momentum is not conserved, because kinetic energy decreased.

subject: AP Physics 1
stem: A 2 kg cart moving at +4 m/s collides with a 1 kg cart at rest on a frictionless track. A student's data show that afterward the 2 kg cart moves at +1 m/s and the 1 kg cart moves at +6 m/s. The carts contain no springs or other stored energy. Which statement about these data is correct?

choices.t: The collision was elastic, because the total momentum is the same before and after.
The data are impossible: momentum balances at 8 kg·m/s, but kinetic energy would rise from 16 J to 19 J.
The collision was inelastic, because the carts end with different speeds.
The collision was perfectly inelastic, because the lighter cart ends up faster.

subject: AP Physics 1
stem: Cart A (1 kg) moves at 4 m/s toward an identical stationary cart B (1 kg) on a frictionless track. In collision 1 the carts stick together. In collision 2 the same carts collide elastically. Which statement correctly compares the two collisions?

choices.t: The total momentum afterward is the same in both (4 kg·m/s), the kinetic energy afterward is 4 J in collision 1 and 8 J in collision 2, and cart B receives half as much impulse in collision 1.
The total momentum afterward is smaller in collision 1, because kinetic energy is lost there.
The kinetic energy afterward is the same in both collisions, because momentum is conserved in both.
The total momentum afterward is the same in both collisions and cart B receives the same impulse in both, because cart A starts with the same momentum.
